cmd:resource|downgrade|drop.comment: this pin function (GYRO_CLKIN or PIOUART) doesn't exist in 4.5.5, so the line was dropped
cmd:resource|downgrade|drop.detail: Resource indexes are 1-based in both versions, and no existing owners were renamed or removed. Only these three new owners can't be expressed in 4.5.5.
cmd:resource|downgrade|drop.note: 2025.12.5 added the resource owners GYRO_CLKIN, PIOUART_TX and PIOUART_RX. 4.5.5 rejects them, so this pin assignment was removed. Hardware that depends on this pin won't be set up in 4.5.5. Check that the build still works without it.

cmd:serial|downgrade|*.comment: port name turned back into a 4.5.5 port number; lines 4.5.5 can't accept are dropped and must be redone
cmd:serial|downgrade|*.detail: PR #13585 and PR #14094 renumbered ports, and 4.5.5 would read any name as port 0, which would overwrite UART1. PR #14192 (GPS 230400) and PR #14697 (telemetry up to 460800) raised speed limits that 4.5.5 caps at 115200. 4.5.5 rejects the whole serial line if a speed is too high, so these lines are dropped rather than clamped.
cmd:serial|downgrade|*.note: 4.5.5 only understands port numbers, so names like UART1 were changed back to numbers (UART1 becomes 0). The converter drops a line if it uses UART0 or a PIOUART port, which 4.5.5 doesn't have, or a GPS or telemetry speed above 115200. The original line stays in the comment, so set that port up again at 115200 or lower.

cmd:serial|downgrade|drop.comment: dropped: either 4.5.5 has no such port, or the GPS/telemetry baud is above 4.5.5's 115200 limit
cmd:serial|downgrade|drop.detail: PRs #13585 and #14094 renumbered the serial ports and added UART0. PR #14192 raised the GPS limit to 230400 and PR #14697 raised the telemetry limit to 460800. The rate isn't clamped, because a device without auto-baud would silently stop working.
cmd:serial|downgrade|drop.note: This port line was removed for one of two reasons. Either the port (UART0 or a PIOUART) doesn't exist in 4.5.5, or its GPS or telemetry baud rate is above 115200, and 4.5.5 rejects the whole line in that case. Your original line is kept in the comment, so you can re-create the port on a 4.5.5 port at 115200 or lower. Set the connected device to the same speed.

cmd:serial|upgrade|*.comment: 2025.12.5 names serial ports instead of numbering them (0 is now UART1); converted automatically
cmd:serial|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13585 and PR #14094 renumbered the internal serial port IDs (UART1 was 0 in 4.5.5 and is 51 in 2025.12.5). 2025.12.5 still accepts the old numbers, but the converter writes names so the output matches a native 2025.12.5 dump.
cmd:serial|upgrade|*.note: 2025.12.5 shows serial ports by name, such as UART1, VCP or SOFT1, instead of the old numbers. Your port number was swapped for the matching name, so the port keeps the same functions and speeds. You don't need to do anything.

feature:OPTICALFLOW|downgrade|*.note: The OPTICALFLOW feature doesn't exist in 4.5.5, so this line was removed. An optical flow sensor connected to the quad won't be used after the downgrade.

set:gyro_to_use|downgrade|*.note: gyro_to_use is set from gyro 1 and gyro 2 in gyro_enabled_bitmask: both on gives BOTH, only gyro 2 gives SECOND, anything else gives FIRST. If you had gyros 3 or higher enabled, or none at all, the result is FIRST, so check that it matches your hardware.

set:iterm_limit|downgrade|*.comment: 4.5.5 has its own iTerm limit setting again; it stays at its default of 400
set:iterm_limit|downgrade|*.detail: PR #13543 removed the iterm_limit setting and made the iTerm limit a percentage (iterm_windup) of pidsum_limit, so a downgrade goes back to the standalone setting.
set:iterm_limit|downgrade|*.note: 2025.12.5 had no separate iterm_limit; the limit came from iterm_windup and pidsum_limit. In 4.5.5 iterm_limit is a standalone setting, left at its default of 400. If you had tuned your iTerm limiting, check it and set it again, e.g. `set iterm_limit = 400`.

set:iterm_limit|upgrade|*.comment: iTerm limit is no longer a separate setting; it now comes from iterm_windup and pidsum_limit
set:iterm_limit|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13543 removed the iterm_limit CLI entry and made the iTerm limit itermWindup% of pidSumLimit, applied per axis.
set:iterm_limit|upgrade|*.note: The standalone iterm_limit setting was dropped, so the line is removed. The limit is now worked out from iterm_windup (a percentage of each axis's pidsum_limit), and iterm_windup now means something different from before, so check its value.

set:iterm_windup|downgrade|*.comment: means motor-saturation threshold in 4.5.5, not a per-axis iTerm cap; reset to the 4.5.5 default of 85
set:iterm_windup|downgrade|*.detail: PR #13543 changed iterm_windup from a motor-saturation windup point to itermLimit = 0.01 * iterm_windup * pidSumLimit. It also changed the minimum from 30 to 20 and the default from 85 to 80.
set:iterm_windup|downgrade|*.note: In 2025.12.5 this is a per-axis iTerm cap, given as a percentage of pidSumLimit. In 4.5.5 it is a motor-mix saturation percentage above which iTerm growth is scaled down on all axes. The same number means something different, so the 4.5.5 default is written: `set iterm_windup = 85`.

set:iterm_windup|upgrade|*.comment: now caps each axis's iTerm as a % of pidSumLimit (replacing iterm_limit); reset to the default of 80
set:iterm_windup|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13543 replaced the motor-saturation windup point with itermLimit = 0.01 * iterm_windup * pidSumLimit (the yaw cap uses pidSumLimitYaw). It also changed the minimum from 30 to 20 and the default from 85 to 80.
set:iterm_windup|upgrade|*.note: In 4.5.5 this was a motor-saturation threshold that scaled back iTerm on all axes at once. In 2025.12.5 it is a per-axis iTerm cap, given as a percentage of that axis's pidSumLimit, and it takes over from the removed iterm_limit. The same number now means something different, so the new default is written: `set iterm_windup = 80`.

set:landing_disarm_threshold|downgrade|*.comment: auto-disarm on landing impact doesn't exist in 4.5.5, so this setting is dropped
set:landing_disarm_threshold|downgrade|*.detail: PR #13803 introduced auto-disarm on landing impact, and PR #13835 later renamed its variables. Neither is in 4.5.5.
set:landing_disarm_threshold|downgrade|*.note: The accelerometer auto-disarm on landing feature was added after 4.5.5, so there is nothing to carry this value to. After the downgrade the craft will not auto-disarm on landing.

set:landing_disarm_threshold|upgrade|*.comment: new auto-disarm on landing impact; it is off by default (0)
set:landing_disarm_threshold|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13803 added the accelerometer auto-disarm on landing impact, and PR #13835 renamed its variables and the CLI setting to landing_disarm_threshold.
set:landing_disarm_threshold|upgrade|*.note: 2025.12.5 can disarm automatically when the accelerometer detects a landing impact. It stays off at the default of 0 until you set a value, in the range 0 to 250, with `set landing_disarm_threshold = <value>`.

set:mag_bustype|downgrade|0.comment: this bus name meant something different in 2025.12.5 and has no clean 4.5.5 match; the board default applies
set:mag_bustype|downgrade|0.detail: From 2025.12, a QSPI bus type was added to the bus-type list without updating the CLI name table. That shifted every name from SLAVE onward by one position. NONE, I2C and SPI mean the same in both versions and carry over.
set:mag_bustype|downgrade|0.note: Because of a naming bug in 2025.12.5, SLAVE there actually stored QSPI (no compass support) and GYROAUTO stored the MPU slave bus. Your line was commented out and the board's own 4.5.5 default applies, which is right for most boards. After flashing, check that your compass is detected.

set:mag_bustype|upgrade|0.comment: this bus name stores a different bus type in 2025.12.5, so it was dropped; the board default applies
set:mag_bustype|upgrade|0.detail: From 2025.12, a QSPI bus type was added to the bus-type list without updating the CLI name table. That shifted every name from SLAVE onward by one position. NONE, I2C and SPI are unaffected and carry over normally.
set:mag_bustype|upgrade|0.note: In 2025.12.5 the compass bus names no longer match the stored values: SLAVE now selects QSPI, which the compass code doesn't support, and GYROAUTO selects the MPU slave bus. Your line was commented out and the board's own default applies, which is right for most boards. After flashing, check that your compass is detected.

set:mag_declination|downgrade|*.comment: negative (west) declinations are written as 360° minus the value, as this version expects
set:mag_declination|downgrade|*.detail: PRs #14019 and #14206 moved mag_declination from an unsigned 0..3599 range to a signed -300..300 range. Going back to 4.5.5, negative values have 3600 added.
set:mag_declination|downgrade|*.note: 4.5.5 has no negative declinations; west values wrap into 0..3599 tenths of a degree instead (e.g. -50 becomes 3550). The converter did this for you, so the heading correction stays the same.

set:mag_declination|upgrade|*.comment: west declinations are now negative numbers instead of wrapping past 360°; values beyond ±30° get clamped
set:mag_declination|upgrade|*.detail: PR #14019 made the field signed and changed the CLI range from 0..3599 to -300..300, and PR #14206 confirmed the signed range. The converter turns values above 1800 into negative numbers and clamps to ±300.
set:mag_declination|upgrade|*.note: Still in tenths of a degree, but west declinations are now stored as negative numbers (e.g. 3550 becomes -50), and the range is limited to -300..300. If your declination was beyond ±30°, it was clamped and your heading will be off; use the closest value you can, e.g. `set mag_declination = 300`.

set:min_throttle|downgrade|*.comment: 4.5.5 sets analog idle with min_throttle; rebuilt here from motor_idle and min_command
set:min_throttle|downgrade|*.detail: PR #13936 removed min_throttle and made analog outputLow = min_command + motor_idle*0.1; this reverses that formula for 4.5.5, where outputLow = min_throttle.
set:min_throttle|downgrade|*.note: 2025.12.5 has no min_throttle; analog/PWM idle comes from min_command plus motor_idle/10. The converter worked out the matching min_throttle so your analog idle level stays the same, limited to the 750-2250 range. Nothing to do unless you want a different idle.

set:min_throttle|upgrade|*.comment: removed; on analog protocols the idle level is now folded into motor_idle, worked out from min_command
set:min_throttle|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13936 removed min_throttle and renamed dshot_idle_value to motor_idle; the analog low endpoint changed from minthrottle to mincommand + motorIdle*0.1.
set:min_throttle|upgrade|*.note: min_throttle no longer exists. On analog (non-DShot) protocols the idle output is now min_command + motor_idle/10, so motor_idle was set to (min_throttle - min_command) x 10, clamped to 0-2000, which gives the same idle level. On DShot or ProShot, motor_idle comes from dshot_idle_value instead, and this value isn't used.

set:motor_idle|upgrade|*.comment: replaces dshot_idle_value (DShot) and min_throttle (analog); value carried over based on your protocol
set:motor_idle|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13936 renamed dshot_idle_value to motor_idle and dropped min_throttle; analog idle is now min_command + motor_idle*0.1. The setting your protocol doesn't use is dropped.
set:motor_idle|upgrade|*.note: In 2025.12.5, motor_idle sets idle for both DShot and analog ESCs. With DShot or PROSHOT1000 it takes your dshot_idle_value unchanged; with other protocols it is calculated as (min_throttle - min_command) x 10, limited to 0-2000, so idle stays the same. A stock brushed setup upgrades to 0, which keeps its old idle rather than the new brushed default.

set:osd_canvas_height|upgrade|*.comment: canvas size is no longer set in the CLI; it now comes from the display, so the line is dropped
set:osd_canvas_height|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13595 wrapped osd_canvas_height in #ifdef OSD_CANVAS_SIZE_DEBUG, so it is gone from normal CLI builds and old values are not restored over the display's canvas.
set:osd_canvas_height|upgrade|*.note: 2025.12.5 builds don't accept this setting, so the line was removed. The OSD canvas size now comes from the display (OSD_SD/OSD_HD or the digital FPV system) at runtime, so there is nothing for you to set again.

set:osd_canvas_width|upgrade|*.comment: canvas size is no longer set in the CLI; it now comes from the display, so the line is dropped
set:osd_canvas_width|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13595 wrapped osd_canvas_width in #ifdef OSD_CANVAS_SIZE_DEBUG, so it is gone from normal CLI builds and old values are not restored over the display's canvas.
set:osd_canvas_width|upgrade|*.note: 2025.12.5 builds don't accept this setting, so the line was removed. The OSD canvas size now comes from the display (OSD_SD/OSD_HD or the digital FPV system) at runtime, so there is nothing for you to set again.

set:pinio_box|downgrade|*.comment: ALTHOLD (3), POS HOLD (11) and CHIRP (55) don't exist in 4.5.5, so those entries become 255 (none)
set:pinio_box|downgrade|*.detail: PR #13816 (ALTHOLD, ID 3), PR #13975 (POS HOLD, ID 11) and PR #13105 (CHIRP, ID 55) added these modes after 4.5.5.
set:pinio_box|downgrade|*.note: Any PINIO pin linked to ALTHOLD, POS HOLD or CHIRP was set to 255, because 4.5.5 has no such modes and the pin would never switch anyway. Other entries carry over unchanged; if you want that pin on another mode, assign it again after loading.

set:pinio_box|upgrade|*.comment: mode IDs 3 and 11 now mean ALTHOLD and POS HOLD, so they're set to 255 (none) to keep the pin off
set:pinio_box|upgrade|*.detail: PR #13816 gave permanent ID 3 to ALTHOLD and PR #13975 gave ID 11 to POS HOLD; both were unused (commented out) in 4.5.5.
set:pinio_box|upgrade|*.note: In 4.5.5, IDs 3 and 11 matched no mode, so a PINIO pin set to them never switched. 2025.12.5 uses them for ALTHOLD and POS HOLD, so they were changed to 255 to keep the pin off as before. All other entries carry over unchanged.

set:prearm_allow_rearm|upgrade|*.comment: New option to allow re-arming without resetting the PreArm switch; it is off by default.
set:prearm_allow_rearm|upgrade|*.detail: PR #14013 added the option to allow re-arming without resetting the PreArm AUX.
set:prearm_allow_rearm|upgrade|*.note: This setting is new and stays at its default of OFF, so arming behaves as before. If you want to re-arm without first toggling the PreArm switch off, set `set prearm_allow_rearm = ON`.

set:rangefinder_hardware|downgrade|0.comment: this rangefinder type doesn't exist in 4.5.5, so the rangefinder is turned off (NONE)
set:rangefinder_hardware|downgrade|0.detail: PR #13980 added the MTF01, MTF02, MTF01P and MTF02P types, and PR #14376 added TFNOVA. Both appended them after the original four types, which keep their meaning.
set:rangefinder_hardware|downgrade|0.note: 4.5.5 only supports the HCSR04, TFMINI and TF02 rangefinders, so your sensor type can't be carried over. The converter wrote `set rangefinder_hardware = NONE`. If you have one of the supported sensors, set it again, e.g. `set rangefinder_hardware = TFMINI`.

set:rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff|down.comment: set equal to rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff to match how 2025.12.5 filtered feedforward
set:rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff|down.detail: PR #14411 merged the feedforward cutoff into rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff and removed rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff.
set:rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff|down.note: 2025.12.5 has no separate feedforward smoothing cutoff; it always uses rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff. The converter copies that value here so feedforward smoothing behaves the same in 4.5.5.

set:rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff|upgr.comment: merged away: feedforward smoothing now always uses the same cutoff as rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff
set:rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff|upgr.detail: PR #14411 removed rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff and combined it with rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff.
set:rc_smoothing_feedforward_cutoff|upgr.note: There's no longer a separate feedforward smoothing cutoff, so this value was dropped. Feedforward now uses rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff, which carries over unchanged. If you had set a feedforward cutoff different from the setpoint cutoff, that difference is lost.

set:serialrx_provider|downgrade|0.comment: MAVLink receiver input doesn't exist in 4.5.5; choose a supported protocol or the receiver won't work
set:serialrx_provider|downgrade|0.detail: PR #14681 added MAVLINK to the end of the serial RX provider list. All other providers are unchanged and carry over.
set:serialrx_provider|downgrade|0.note: 4.5.5 cannot read a receiver over MAVLink, so your line was commented out and the board's own default protocol applies. Unless your receiver can output another protocol, you will have no control link. Set your receiver to a protocol 4.5.5 supports and select it, e.g. `set serialrx_provider = CRSF`. Then check that the receiver responds before flying.

set:system_hse_mhz|downgrade|0.comment: 4.5.5 can't use a 26 MHz crystal on STM32G4 boards, so the board's own default is used instead
set:system_hse_mhz|downgrade|0.detail: PR #14261 added 26 MHz support to the STM32G4 systemClockSetHSEValue in 2025.12. Before that, a guard returned early for 26, so the value was silently ignored.
set:system_hse_mhz|downgrade|0.note: 4.5.5 ignores a 26 MHz external crystal setting on STM32G4 boards. The CLI text doesn't say which MCU your board has, so your line was commented out on every board and the board's default applies. If your board isn't STM32G4 and really uses a 26 MHz crystal, you can set it again with `set system_hse_mhz = 26`.

set:thr_hover|downgrade|*.comment: 4.5.5 has no separate hover point; the curve's midpoint output always equals thr_mid, so this is dropped
set:thr_hover|downgrade|*.detail: PR #14229 split the old single midpoint into thr_mid (stick position) and thr_hover (throttle output). 4.5.5 only has the combined point, so it can't express thr_hover separately.
set:thr_hover|downgrade|*.note: In 4.5.5, thr_mid sets both the stick position and the throttle output at the curve's midpoint, so thr_hover can't be carried over. Your thr_mid value is kept. If your thr_hover was different from thr_mid, the middle of your throttle curve will feel different, so check your hover throttle after flashing.

set:thr_hover|upgrade|*.comment: new curve-midpoint output setting, set equal to your thr_mid so your throttle curve stays the same
set:thr_hover|upgrade|*.detail: PR #14229 split the throttle curve midpoint into thr_mid and thr_hover, and the curve now passes through (thr_mid, thr_hover).
set:thr_hover|upgrade|*.note: thr_mid used to set both the stick position and the output of the throttle curve's midpoint. Those are now split into thr_mid (stick position) and thr_hover (output). thr_hover was set to your old thr_mid value, so your throttle curve is unchanged.

set:thr_mid|downgrade|*.comment: kept as the stick position; in 4.5.5 it also sets the midpoint output, so any separate thr_hover is lost
set:thr_mid|downgrade|*.detail: PR #14229 split the 4.5.5 midpoint into thr_mid (x) and thr_hover (y), and PR #14356 kept that split. Going back to 4.5.5 means the curve can only pass through thr_mid on both axes.
set:thr_mid|downgrade|*.note: Your thr_mid value is kept. 4.5.5 has no thr_hover, so the throttle output at the curve's midpoint will equal thr_mid. If your thr_hover was different, the middle of your throttle curve will change, so check your hover throttle after flashing.

set:thr_mid|upgrade|*.comment: now only sets the stick position; thr_hover is set to the same value so your throttle curve stays the same
set:thr_mid|upgrade|*.detail: PR #14229 made thr_mid the x-coordinate of the curve midpoint and added thr_hover as the y-coordinate. PR #14356 still builds the curve through (thr_mid, thr_hover).
set:thr_mid|upgrade|*.note: In 4.5.5, thr_mid set both the stick position and the throttle output of the curve's midpoint. In 2025.12.5 the output is a separate setting, thr_hover. Your thr_mid value is kept, and thr_hover is set to the same number, so the curve behaves exactly as before.

set:tpa_low_rate|downgrade|*.comment: 4.5.5 has no negative values (PID boost at low throttle); those become 0, and 0-100 carries over
set:tpa_low_rate|downgrade|*.detail: PR #13661 changed tpa_low_rate to a signed value that can go down to -128 on USE_WING builds. PR #13778 did not change its units.
set:tpa_low_rate|downgrade|*.note: Newer wing builds allow negative tpa_low_rate to boost PIDs at low throttle, but 4.5.5 only accepts 0 to 100. A negative value is set to 0, which means no low-throttle TPA. Values from 0 to 100 are kept unchanged.

set:tpa_mode|downgrade|0.comment: PDS mode doesn't exist in 4.5.5, so this was reset to the default D mode
set:tpa_mode|downgrade|0.detail: PR #14010 added the PDS value (wing builds only) alongside wing setpoint attenuation. 4.5.5 only offers PD and D.
set:tpa_mode|downgrade|0.note: The PDS TPA mode, which also attenuates the S-term, was added after 4.5.5 and has nothing equivalent there. Your line was commented out and replaced with `set tpa_mode = D`, the 4.5.5 default. If you'd rather use PD, enter `set tpa_mode = PD`, and check your TPA tuning before you fly.
